q.intro.text: A bag holds four marbles: three blue and one white. You reach in without looking and pull one out.

q.ask.text: How likely is it that you pull a blue marble?

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the notation.

e.s1.text: Every marble gets its own name: B one, B two, B three, and W. These four outcomes are the sample space.

e.s2.text: The marbles are the same size and well mixed, so each one is equally likely: one fourth each. The colors are not: there are more blue marbles.

e.s3.text: The event blue is made of three outcomes: B one, B two, and B three. Three of the four.

e.s4.text: P of blue is three fourths: the blue outcomes on top, all the outcomes underneath. On the scale from zero to one, that is likely, not certain.

e.why.text: Quick check. There are only two colors. Why isn't the chance of blue one half?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. The marbles are what is equally likely, and three of the four are blue.

e.w-eq.text: Two colors don't make it fifty-fifty. Blue and white are not equally likely: blue has three marbles, white has one.

e.w-part.text: Three to one compares blue with white. A probability compares blue with all the marbles: three of four.

t.intro.text: Now the bag holds six marbles: two blue, three white, and one pink. What is the chance the marble is not white? The first two steps are done for you.

t.given.text: Six marbles, six names, and each one is equally likely: one sixth each. Your turn.

t.count.text: Which marbles make up the event not white? Tap every one, then check.

t.c-ok.text: Yes: B one, B two, and P. Three outcomes.

t.c-white.text: Not white means every marble that is not white. Leave the white ones out.

t.c-miss.text: Some are missing. Every marble that is not white is in the event, the pink one too.

t.c-one.text: An event can hold more than one outcome. Tap every marble that is not white.

t.write.text: Now write the chance of not white as a fraction.

t.w-ok.text: Yes: three of the six marbles. Three sixths.

t.w-colors.text: That counts colors: two of the three colors. The colors are not equally likely; the marbles are. Count marbles.

t.w-part.text: That compares with the white marbles. Compare with all six marbles.

t.w-count.text: Three is how many marbles are in the event. A probability says out of how many: put all the marbles underneath.

t.w-other.text: Count the marbles in the event for the top, and all the marbles for the bottom.

t.place.text: Where does it go on the scale?

t.p-ok.text: Right. Three sixths is one half: as likely as not.

t.p-no.text: Three sixths is exactly one half: the middle of the scale.

t.cb-eq.text: At the start you picked one half for blue: that counted colors. Here the answer is one half, but because three of the six marbles count, not because there are two ways.

t.cb-right.text: At the start you picked three fourths, and you were right. Now you can show why: count the marbles, not the colors.

t.cb-part.text: At the start you picked three to one. That compares blue with white. A probability compares with all the marbles: three fourths.

t.cb-none.text: At the start: three of the four marbles are blue, so the chance of blue is three fourths.

p.intro.text: Sam uses the first bag: three blue and one white. Sam pulls a marble, puts it back and mixes, four times: blue, white, blue, white. Sam says: the chance of blue is really one half, so three fourths was wrong. Is Sam right?

p.yes.text: Let's test it. Build the argument and see where it leads.

p.no.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.c1.text: Ten batches of four draws: the number of blues jumps around, and two blues is nothing unusual.

p.c2.text: Four hundred draws: the share of blue wanders at first, then settles close to three fourths.

p.c3.text: A probability describes the long run. Four draws can't overturn three fourths.

p.x-mirror.text: Four draws don't have to give exactly three blue. The batches show it: they jump around.

p.x-closer.text: Not every draw: the share can wander away for a while. It settles only over many draws.

p.x-due.text: Nothing is due: the marble goes back and the bag is mixed. Every draw is three fourths for blue.

p.x-other.text: True, but it backs a different line. Which reason makes this line true?

p.done.text: That's a proof: three claims, each with its reason, and the picture backs every one. Sam judged a probability by four draws.
